episodes.title: Punished for Doing Her Duty as a State Worker.

blocks.text:
Bhanwari Devi was employed by the Rajasthan Government as a social worker (Saathin) under the Women’s Development Project.

In 1992, while preventing the child marriage of a nine-month-old infant in Bhateri village, she was brutally gang-raped by influential upper-caste men.

FACTUAL MATRIX (Statement of Facts): Bhanwari Devi was employed by the Rajasthan Government as a social worker (Saathin) under the Women’s Development Project.

In 1992, while preventing the child marriage of a nine-month-old infant in Bhateri village, she was brutally gang-raped by influential upper-caste men. The legal controversy originated from whether the act committed fell within the statutory exceptions.

episodes.title: A Shocking Trial Court Acquittal Triggers National Fury.

blocks.text:
In 1995, a Sessions Court acquitted all the accused with shocking remarks, claiming "elderly village men of high caste would not rape a lower caste woman".

Outraged by the systemic misogyny, women rights advocates united under the collective name "Vishaka" and approached the Supreme Court directly under Article 32.

episodes.title: 13 August 1997: The Vishaka Guidelines are Born.

blocks.text:
A 3-judge bench led by CJI J.S. Verma delivered a masterpiece of judicial statesmanship:

1. **Defined Sexual Harassment**: Unwelcome physical contact, demands for sexual favours, sexually coloured remarks, showing pornography.
2. **Mandated Internal Complaints Committees (ICC)**: Every organization with 10+ employees must have an ICC headed by a woman.
3. **Universal Applicability**: Binding on all private and public sector workplaces across India under Article 141.

episodes.title: From Judicial Decree to the POSH Act 2013.

blocks.text:
The Vishaka Guidelines operated as the supreme law of the land for 16 years.

In 2013, Parliament formally codified these principles into **The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 (POSH Act)**.

Today, millions of working women across India are protected because of one case that refused to be silenced.

flashcards.q: Which court decided Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan and in what year?
flashcards.a: Supreme Court of India in the year 1997.

flashcards.q: What was the primary legal issue addressed in this case?
What is the core Ratio Decidendi of the judgment?
flashcards.a: The Supreme Court held that workplace sexual harassment is a direct violation of fundamental rights to gender equality and personal liberty under Articles 14 and 21. The Court formulated the binding "Vishaka Guidelines" and mandated the creation of Internal Complaints Committees (ICC) across all workplaces.

flashcards.q: What is the primary citation for this ruling?
flashcards.a: Vishaka and others v. State of Rajasthan, (1997) 6 SCC 241, AIR 1997 SC 3011

flashcards.q: What is the current legal status of this precedent?
flashcards.a: Vishaka judicial guidelines were codified into legislation by the POSH Act 2013.
